transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-09
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: see metadata above

Summary:
Quick walk through the customer's SIG v2.2 vendor risk questionnaire and where evidence lives. Primary concerns: encryption & KMS, data residency for EU customers, RBAC/SSO integrations, and audit log retention for 12+ months. Redwood AE+SE pair present; legal/procurement and cloud architects from Cedar on call.

Topics covered:
- SIG/CAIQ mapping and gaps
- SOC 2 evidence and timing for report delivery
- KMS key management (BYOK options) and HSM integration
- VPC/private deployment footprint and audit logs
- Timeline for evidence collection and PoC

Transcript body (timestamps are approximate, automated notes with occasional mis-transcriptions):

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, I'm the account lead on this. We've got Diego and Samira from our security and product teams. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Priya Nambiar: Good, thanks. We put together the vendor risk team for this—I'm Priya, head of IT Risk. Ethan and Janelle on the call as well.
[00:12] Diego Alvarez: Hey all. We'll go through the SIG workbook and call out which sections are usually a blocker and what artifacts help close them.
[00:19] Ethan Ross: Sounds good. For context, Cedar runs a mix of EU and US workloads. Data residency is our first gating item. We also need RBAC to map to our existing SSO/SAML roles.
[00:28] Maya Chen: Right. We'll flag the residency-related SIG items and show where our evidence sits. Quick note — the automated transcript may spell KMS as 'K M S' in places, sorry for noise.

[02:10] Samira Ford: Jumping in on SOC 2 — we are SOC 2 Type II and our report cycles are quarterly for controls changes. We can provide the most recent report once NDA is in place. The typical ask I see: explicit list of scoping notes, plus the control mapping to SIG questions.
[02:34] Marco Silva: Is the SOC 2 report going to cover private deployments as well? We need to be explicit for any on-prem installs.
[02:41] Samira Ford: Good question. Our hosted Redwood API is covered in the SOC scope. For Private (VPC/on-prem) we provide a control alignment pack and evidence where applicable, but full SOC coverage depends on customer-managed components. We'll include scope notes in the evidence bundle.

[05:00] Janelle Park: From procurement side — timeline wise, we need a completed SIG and supporting evidence within two weeks to feed legal. Can you meet that?
[05:09] Maya Chen: Yes — we'll upload a prefilled SIG workbook with evidence links and notes by Monday 2025-10-13. That will include artifacts for encryption, RBAC, SSO, and logs.

[07:50] Diego Alvarez: On encryption and KMS, there are two common patterns: Redwood-managed KMS (we manage keys in our cloud provider KMS) and Customer BYOK (bring-your-own-key) where keys are in customer's KMS/HSM. For audit logs we produce tamper-evident logs and can export to customer SIEM via syslog or cloud export.
[08:12] Ethan Ross: For BYOK — does Redwood support keys in our Azure Key Vault and customer rotation? We need HSM-backed keys.
[08:20] Diego Alvarez: Yes. We support BYOK with HSM-backed key stores (Azure Key Vault, AWS CloudHSM, and also integrations with on-prem HSMs via KMIP in some deployments). We'll note the exact certs and flows in the evidence packet.

[10:05] Naomi Trent: One practical ask: we need to confirm encryption at rest for cached KV and for any S3-like object storage used for model artifacts.
[10:15] Liam O'Neill: We encrypt KV cache and model artifacts at rest with AES-256. For dedicated pools we can also enable customer-managed keys. We'll include the cryptographic algorithm details in the evidence doc.

[12:30] Priya Nambiar: On RBAC and SSO — we use SAML 2.0 with role mapping today. Can you show how Redwood maps token claims to internal roles and how access revocation works if a user is deprovisioned?
[12:45] Diego Alvarez: We map SAML/SCIM attributes to RBAC roles. SCIM provisioning is supported for user lifecycle and immediate deprovisioning. For sessions, tokens are short-lived and we invalidate sessions on deprovision. We'll attach our SSO integration guide and example SAML assertions.

[15:05] Marco Silva: A lot of our controls team asks for sample audit logs showing authentication events, admin actions, and key rotations. Can you provide redacted samples?
[15:15] Samira Ford: Absolutely — redacted audit log samples are part of the standard evidence bundle. They show timestampts, subject, action, resource, and outcome. We'll provide a schema and an example.

[18:40] Ethan Ross: Data residency details — we need to know physical regions where data can be stored and if any PII is ever replicated outside the chosen region for backups or DR.
[18:52] Maya Chen: We offer region pinning for EU, US, and APAC. Backups and DR are region-aware; any cross-region replication is opt-in and documented. For the SIG items, we'll include a region map and our data flow diagrams.

[21:00] Janelle Park: On the SIG workbook itself — which sections do you usually leave for the customer to confirm vs the vendor to fill?
[21:08] Diego Alvarez: We'll prefill about 70-80% with vendor-covered controls (infrastructure, platform controls). Customer-responsibility items — e.g., application-layer encryption for customer-managed keys or specific workload configs — we'll mark 'customer-managed' and add guidance.

[24:30] Priya Nambiar: For audit retention — Cedar requires 12 months immutable logs and 3 years metadata. What's Redwood's default?
[24:40] Samira Ford: Default is 13 months for full audit logs and 3 years for compressed event indices; we can extend retention via enterprise add-on. We'll note retention SLAs and why they meet the 12-month requirement.

[28:10] Naomi Trent: Can you run a check to ensure that any PII is not included in transcripts or debug logs that are stored? We need assurances about redaction.
[28:20] Liam O'Neill: We have automated redaction for user-submitted content in logs, and access to raw content is restricted to a small set of roles with approval workflows. We'll include the redaction policy and role list.

[31:00] Marco Silva: Legal side — we need to confirm indemnity language and data processing addendum (DPA) for EU customers. Is your standard DPA compatible with our requirements?
[31:10] Maya Chen: Our legal team has a standard DPA that covers data processing terms and SCCs. For larger deals, we can negotiate additional clauses; we typically surface DPA language during contract talks. We'll flag this to our legal counterpart and copy you.

[34:45] Diego Alvarez: A few SIG-specific notes: for CAIQ items around multi-tenancy isolation, we include network segmentation diagrams, tenant isolation checks, and process descriptions. Some automated transcript lines might read 'multi tenancy' as one word — ignore that.

[36:30] Ethan Ross: One of the CAIQ items asks for penetration test cadence and third-party assessor names. Can you list the last three assessors and dates?
[36:40] Samira Ford: Yes — we'll include the last three pentesters and summaries/redacted reports where commerical confidentiality allows. We'll also provide cert of remediation for any findings closed in the last cycle.

[39:50] Janelle Park: Back to practical next steps: we need the SIG workbook, SOC 2 report, redacted audit logs, SSO integration guide, and KMS integration docs. Anything else?
[40:00] Maya Chen: We'll also attach the region map, dataflow diagram, and a short guide for customer-managed key rotations and evidence list for on-prem/private deployments.

[42:10] Priya Nambiar: Can we schedule a short follow-up specifically scoped to BYOK + VPC PoC? Our cloud team wants to validate network egress rules.
[42:18] Diego Alvarez: Yes — Diego to run the PoC with Ethan and Naomi the week of 2025-10-20. We'll prepare a checklist.

[44:25] Maya Chen: Final recap: Redwood to upload evidence bundle and prefilled SIG by 2025-10-13. Cedar to review and surface any blockers; if PoC needed we'll kick that off week of 2025-10-20. Action items and owners in the meeting notes.
[44:45] Marco Silva: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[44:50] Priya Nambiar: Thanks, appreciate it.

Notes about transcription quality: several product/tech acronyms sometimes spaced ("S O C 2", "K M S", "C A I Q"), occasional speaker mis-attribution at turn boundaries due to call joining.

Shared artifacts referenced (short notes):
- Prefilled SIG workbook and evidence bundle (will be uploaded by Redwood to shared folder)
- SSO/SCIM integration guide (redwood.docs/ssoguides - placeholder link)
- KMS/BYOK integration notes (attached in evidence package)
- Region map and data-flow diagrams (attached)

End of transcript.
